transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-01-17
Start: 14:00 ET
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya, Ethan, Rosa (AmberLane) + legal hinted as Speaker 1

---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, I'm Maya Chen from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: Priya Desai, Head of Cloud Eng at AmberLane. We're focusing on payments orchestration and we have strict controls for logs and keys.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan Mallory, Security Architect, I'll be focused on KMS, audit trails, e-discovery.
[00:20] Rosa: Rosa Jimenez, Compliance. Looking for GDPR plus financial regs coverage.
[00:24] Liam: Liam Ortega, Solutions Engineer at Redwood. I'll walk through hosting options and technical constraints.
[00:30] Speaker 1: (muffled) legal side, hi.

[02:05] Priya: To start, our big Q is where data will sit — we operate in multi-region EU + US, and we need to make sure customer PII never leaves the appropriate jurisdiction. We also have retention rules, sometimes we need to hold logs for up to 7 years, and occasionally we have legal holds that supersede normal retention.
[02:25] Maya: Totally, great context. Short answer: Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem). Each has different controls — we should map them to your control set.

[03:10] Liam: For Hosted, our standard is multi-tenant with region pins, we can restrict model inference to eu-west, etc. But for strict residency and key custody you probably want Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools in our infra, tenant-level logs, and can be region-locked. Private gives you full control — VPC peering or on-prem so keys never leave your vault.

[04:05] Ethan: Clarifying: when you say Dedicated, where do the keys live? Are they in Redwood's KMS or can we bring our own?
[04:12] Liam: You can bring your own KMS (BYOK). For Dedicated we integrate with your KMS via customer-managed key rotation and optional HSM-backed keystores — the key material can be in your cloud provider's KMS; Redwood never stores raw key material.

[04:45] Rosa: How about logs? We need to ensure logs don't capture raw PII, and we need redact/redaction at ingestion. Also separation of access — audit trails per user.
[04:55] Maya: Yep. We can configure log redaction filters and tokenization at the edge. There's an ingestion-stage scrub — you can set patterns for account numbers, names, etc. By default Hosted collects aggregated latency/cost metrics but PII-masking is available as an opt-in.

[06:00] Priya: Is that masking deterministic? We have downstream systems doing joins for troubleshooting but they need pseudo-identifiers.
[06:08] Liam: We support deterministic pseudonymization so you can preserve join-keys without keeping raw PII in logs. That mapping can be stored in your KMS-backed store or in your VPC-only storage if you pick Private.

[07:00] Ethan: And legal hold? If we get a subpoena we need to freeze some logs and retain them beyond retention windows and export them to our e-discovery system.
[07:10] Maya: We have a legal-hold flagging mechanism. For Dedicated and Private you can set hold policies — Redwood will prevent deletion and export a signed bundle to your S3/GCS bucket. For Hosted, legal hold is supported but needs explicit contract terms and we use partner workflows.

[08:00] Rosa: GDPR data subject request — can we do right-to-be-forgotten when interactions were processed by a model?
[08:07] Liam: It's nuanced. If you don't store the prompt/response in the logs (masking on), then there's less to delete. For stored items, we can identify and redact or delete artifacts. For model weights–derived info, well, that's not identifiable. We provide a chain-of-custody and deletion attestations.

[09:25] Priya: Performance: our flows require sub-600ms p99 for certain retry paths. How does that change across hosting options?
[09:33] Maya: Hosted gives best time-to-value but worst-case p99 depends on multi-tenant load; we publish profiles. Dedicated gives predictable p99 and you can reserve capacity to hit SLOs. Private on-prem can be tuned to be lowest-latency but you take on ops overhead.

[10:45] Ethan: What about fallback? If Dedicated capacity is exhausted, can requests failover to a hosted model in a different region? That might be a hard no for us.
[10:55] Liam: Failover policies are configurable. You can set strict region-only routing and no cross-region fallback. Alternatively, you can allow fallback to a lower-trust tier but that would require contract-level agreement.

[12:20] Rosa: Audit proofs: we need tamper-evident logs and signed attestations for deletion or export actions. Do you support append-only storage with timestamps?
[12:30] Liam: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we write audit events to an append-only ledger and support export of signed manifests. Hosted has an audit trail but for regulated financial use-cases we recommend Dedicated or Private so you control retention and audit storage.

[13:40] Priya: Network topology — can we route inference traffic through our VPC with NAT?
[13:48] Liam: With Private you get VPC peering; with Dedicated we offer VPC egress IP ranges and peering options. Hosted is public endpoints with TLS and IP allowlists.

[15:00] Priya: We run periodic penetration tests — are there red team controls or can we scan the endpoints?
[15:07] Maya: We coordinate scans for Dedicated/Private; Hosted scans are on our side and we can share pen-test reports (SOC2 scope). We'll need scope and timing.

[16:30] Ethan: Logging verbosity — we'd like per-request metadata including model variant, kernel/quantization profile used, inference node id for triage. Is that captured?
[16:40] Liam: We include model variant, quantization tag, sequence length distribution, routing policy decisions. Node IDs can be recorded in Dedicated and Private logs, less so for Hosted because of shared infra. Some of those fields are heuristics and occasionally mis-typed in the pipeline — e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed in our internal logs as "K V cash" in old stacks, we've fixed that in the new runtime.

[18:05] Priya: How do you handle model caching and prefix caching? If caching stores snippets of user messages does that violate our data policy?
[18:13] Liam: Caching can be configured for TTL and filtering. You can set skip-cache on sensitive routes. For Dedicated/Private you can opt for KV cache encryption and ephemeral caches that are rotated and scrubbed on policy.

[19:20] Rosa: Encryption in transit and at rest? Are there options for customer-managed encryption keys for object storage of logs and also envelope encryption of model artifacts?
[19:28] Maya: TLS in transit, at-rest encryption by default. Customer-managed keys (CMK) supported for both logs and model artifact storage in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we support BYOK but some storage layers still require controlled access; we'll share the whitepaper.

[21:00] Priya: There's also the question of vendor lock — if we needed to move off Redwood, how portable are logs and models?
[21:08] Liam: Logs and audit manifests are exportable as signed bundles (S3/GCS). Model artifacts are standard formats; we can provide tooling to export KV cache snapshots and prompt/response bundles. Private is most portable since you control the runtime.

[22:45] Ethan: Ok specific ask: we want to do a Dedicated pilot in eu-west with BYOK, deterministic pseudonymization, and a 2-week benchmark of p50/p90/p99. Is that feasible?
[22:58] Maya: Yes, that's the usual path. We'll size a small Dedicated pool, run synthetic and real traffic with redaction in place, and measure latency and cost.

[23:20] Priya: For the benchmark we'll need to ingest some synthetic payment transcripts — any guidance on sanitization?
[23:28] Liam: We'll provide a guidance doc. Ideally you strip direct identifiers and keep join keys as pseudonyms. We can also run a small sanitizer job before ingestion.

[25:00] Speaker 1: (legal) on contracts — our procurement requires explicit SLA clauses for data residency and no-comms fallback.
[25:08] Maya: We'll loop in sales ops. Dedicated contracts usually include region-lock and data residency clauses; Private gets stronger guarantees.

[26:30] Rosa: One more: monitoring retention — our auditors want proof we didn't keep transcripts beyond X days, periodically.
[26:40] Liam: We can provide retention manifests and deletion attestations. We also offer alerts when retention anomalies are detected.

[27:55] Priya: Can we segregate logs per business line inside Dedicated? We have different teams with different access levels.
[28:05] Liam: Yes, RBAC is supported. You can do per-route tokens, per-team views, and policy-based access with SSO (SAML/Okta).

[29:30] Ethan: Any regulatory oddities for payments? Financial regs sometimes want immutable records for audit. How do you reconcile immutability with deletion requests?
[29:40] Rosa: (interject) yeah, if there's an audit hold that trumps deletion, so those cases need to be handled.
[29:45] Maya: Right — legal hold overrides deletion. We keep a manifest and can flag records. For immutable audit we write to append-only storage and tag the time and signer.

[31:00] Priya: Do you have customers in market with similar constraints? Reference checks would help.
[31:06] Maya: We've done Dedicated/private with several banks and payments providers; we'll share a sanitized case study.

[32:20] Liam: Technical nuance: quantized models may have slightly different output distributions — does AmberLane have a quality bar for model deltas?
[32:30] Priya: Yes, NLP regression tolerance is strict — we have canary tests against production prompts. If you do quantization we need evals tied to prompt sets and automatic rollback.

[33:10] Liam: Redwood Optimize can run those checks and integrate into rollout policies; canary + auto-fallback is possible. We'll include that in the pilot plan.

[34:25] Ethan: About logs again — we need to ensure certain debug traces aren't shipped off-platform, how do we limit that?
[34:32] Liam: Control plane telemetry is separated from customer logs. Debug traces can be turned off or scrubbed; for Dedicated/Private you get full control.

[36:00] Priya: Cost question: Dedicated reserved capacity — do we commit monthly and can we burst?
[36:09] Maya: There are commit tiers. You can have baseline reserved capacity and burst to Hosted for ephemeral spikes (if you allow fallback). Burst costs more but avoids permanent overprovisioning.

[37:40] Rosa: We also need SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for user accounts and role-based access.
[37:48] Liam: Supported — Okta, Azure AD, and others. SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle.

[39:00] Priya: For the pilot, what telemetry will you provide? Token-level cost, per-route latency, model variance?
[39:09] Liam: We'll deliver per-request traces, token-cost breakdowns, model variant and quantization tag, and a dashboard for the pilot. We'll also provide a trace export for your SREs.

[40:20] Maya: Let's recap next steps quickly. Action items we logged: share SOC2 and KMS whitepaper, Liam to size Dedicated and propose pilot test plan, AmberLane to share sample sanitized traffic and compliance checklist.

[41:05] Priya: Sounds good. One ask — can you include the exact retention-control APIs we can call for programmatic deletion and legal hold?
[41:12] Liam: Yes, we'll include API docs and a sample curl/script.

[42:00] Rosa: Also include a short note on indemnities around cross-border data transfer. That's a legal must.
[42:08] Maya: We'll flag that for legal ops.

[43:15] Speaker 1: (soft) procurement will want a standard template for SLA addenda.
[43:22] Maya: Noted — we'll surface contract language examples.

[44:00] Priya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after we get the pilot plan and docs.
[44:07] Maya: Thanks, AmberLane team. We'll send the artifacts and proposed dates.

---
Meeting end: ~14:48 ET
